$ xref find

by Alexander Panasenko · xrefcode.com

Functions satisfying multiple predicates in one parallel pass.

Intersects string refs, callees, immediate constants, struct displacements, panic source paths, and byte-size bounds in one rayon pass.

Usage

xref find [OPTIONS]

Arguments and options

Options

--calls <CALLS>
Function calls or tail-jumps to ADDR (repeatable).
--refs <REFS>
Function references string or hex address (repeatable).
--imm <IMM>
Function uses immediate constant N (repeatable).
--store
Only mov [mem], imm stores for --imm.
--cmp
Only cmp instructions for --imm.
--disp <DISP>
Function accesses struct field at displacement OFF (repeatable).
--write
Only memory writes for --disp.
--lea
Only lea address-of uses for --disp.
--src <SRC>
Function references panic Location matching PATTERN (repeatable).
--size <SIZE>
Function byte size range (MIN..MAX, MIN.., ..MAX, or EXACT).
--any <ANY>
Minimum number of predicates to satisfy (default: all); ranks by match count.
--back <BACK>
Bytes before each --refs string to include in reachability window.
default 16
--insn <INSN>
Instruction mnemonic with optional Intel operand glob (repeatable).
--class <CLASS>
Instruction class; currently float (repeatable).

Examples

All examples were recorded on public binaries; see Provenance.

Reading the output

  • One line per function that satisfies the predicates: its range and size, then (matched/total: …) with the first witness of each predicate (the instruction or reference that satisfied it).
  • The last line counts the functions. --any K accepts functions matching at least K predicates.

Limits

  • Predicates are evaluated per function on instruction evidence; a string reached only through a callee does not count for the caller.

Provenance

Recorded with a development build of xref after 0.4.0 on Linux x86-64, on xref.stripped = a stripped xref build (the binary of the home-page examples). Output is unchanged; long outputs are cut where marked. <!-- /xref -->
